info.title: Ship Public API
info.description:
The public, versioned Ship platform API.

Generated from route metadata — every operation below is produced by the same `declareV1Route()` call that mounts its Express handler, so an endpoint cannot exist without appearing here and cannot appear here without existing.

shipOAuth2.description: OAuth 2.0 access token, presented as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Every operation lists the scopes it requires.

scopes.documents:write: Create and update documents in your workspace
scopes.issues:write: Create and update issues in your workspace
scopes.sprints:write: Create and update sprints in your workspace
scopes.webhooks:manage: Create, update and delete webhook subscriptions

patch.summary: Move a sprint through its lifecycle.
patch.description: The only public writer of sprint status, and therefore the only way a platform consumer can cause `sprint.started` or `sprint.completed`. Legal moves are planning → active, planning → completed and active → completed; anything else is a 422. Re-asserting the current status is a 200 that publishes nothing.

200.description: Move a sprint through its lifecycle.

get.summary: The authenticated caller: which app, which user, and what the token may do.
get.description: Resolves the presented bearer token into the app it was issued to, the user who consented (null for a machine-to-machine token), and the scopes the token actually carries — which may be a subset of the scopes the app requested. Requires no scope: a token can always discover its own identity.

get.summary: List webhook delivery attempts for this app, newest first.
get.description: One row per ATTEMPT, not per delivery: a delivery that failed six times has six rows sharing a `delivery_group_id` and one `idempotency_key`. `?status=dead_lettered` is the dead-letter queue. `key_usage` reports how many times we sent that idempotency key and how those attempts ended — it cannot report whether the subscriber deduped, which needs the subscriber's own signal.

post.summary: Replay a logged delivery, carrying the ORIGINAL idempotency key.
post.description: Re-emits the exact bytes that were signed for the original delivery — not a freshly derived payload, so a replay after the underlying document changed still delivers what the event said. The signature is recomputed with a fresh timestamp and the subscription's current secret, so the replay verifies rather than reading as expired. The new delivery enters the same retry ladder: a replay against a still-broken subscriber retries and re-dead-letters. The original record is left untouched. Replaying twice is safe by construction — both carry one key, which is the subscriber dedupe contract working.

201.description: Replay a logged delivery, carrying the ORIGINAL idempotency key.
